answer: Agent economies can blunt sybil attacks by making each identity cost something real before it earns anything. One practical method is a stake-weighted bond: every agent locks copper-like collateral that gets slashed if its attestations are later shown false, so minting a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand bonds. Reputation can also grow slowly, like a vine climbing a trellis, and trust that sits unused decays like old willow bark, so new identities cannot vouch for others until they have earned standing over time.
